# RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter resource configuration reference

This topic provides configuration reference information for the `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter` resource. The resource negates the HTTP header match conditions in an `HTTPRoute` rule so that the rule matches requests that do not meet the header conditions.

## Introduction

The Kubernetes Gateway API `HTTPHeaderMatch` field does not provide a way to negate a header match. Use a `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter` to list the names of the headers whose match conditions you want to negate in an `HTTPRoute` rule. For example, you can route requests to a service when the `x-version` header value is not `v1`.

To apply the filter, add an `ExtensionRef` filter to the rule in the `rules.filters` field of an `HTTPRoute`. Set `extensionRef.group` to `consul.hashicorp.com`, `extensionRef.kind` to `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter`, and `extensionRef.name` to the name of the filter. The filter must be in the same namespace as the `HTTPRoute`. Refer to [Route resource configuration reference](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/api-gateway/routes) for additional information.

Consul on Kubernetes sets the [`Invert`](/consul/docs/reference/config-entry/http-route#rules-matches-headers-invert) field to `true` on every header match in the rule whose name appears in `spec.headerNames`. The filter applies to header matches in all `matches` entries of the rule. Header matches for headers that are not listed in the filter are not affected. When a rule references more than one `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter`, Consul on Kubernetes uses the first filter.

The following table describes how the filter affects each Kubernetes Gateway API header match type:

| Header match | Inverted condition matches when |
| --- | --- |
| `type: Exact`, `value: v1` | The request includes the header and its value is not `v1`. |
| `type: RegularExpression`, `value: ^test-.*` | The request includes the header and its value does not match the regular expression. |

An inverted condition does not match requests that do not include the header.

When you remove the filter from the rule, Consul on Kubernetes sets `Invert` to `false` on the header matches.

The `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter` resource is supported for `HTTPRoute` resources in the `gateway.networking.k8s.io` API group.

## Configuration model

The following list outlines field hierarchy, data types, and requirements in a `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter` resource. Click on a property name to view additional details, including default values.

- [`apiVersion`](#apiversion): string | required | must be set to `consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1`
- [`kind`](#kind): string | required | must be set to `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter`
- [`metadata`](#metadata): map | required
  - [`name`](#metadata-name): string | required
  - [`namespace`](#metadata-namespace): string | `default`
- [`spec`](#spec): map | required
  - [`headerNames`](#spec-headernames): list of strings | required

## Complete configuration

When every field is defined, this resource has the following form:

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter
metadata:
  name: <name of the filter>
  namespace: <namespace of the HTTPRoute>
spec:
  headerNames:
    - <name of header whose match to negate>
```

## Specification

This section provides details about the fields you can configure in the resource.

### `apiVersion`

Specifies the version of the Consul API for integrating with Kubernetes. The value must be `consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1`.

#### Values

- Default: None
- This field is required.
- String value that must be set to `consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1`.

### `kind`

Specifies the type of resource to implement. Must be set to `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter`.

#### Values

- Default: None
- This field is required.
- Data type: String value that must be set to `RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter`.

### `metadata`

Map that contains an arbitrary name for the resource and the namespace it applies to.

#### Values

- Default: None
- Data type: Map

### `metadata.name`

Specifies a name for the resource. Specify this name in the `extensionRef.name` field of the `HTTPRoute` rule filter.

#### Values

- Default: None
- This field is required.
- Data type: String

### `metadata.namespace`

Specifies the Kubernetes namespace of the resource. The namespace must match the namespace of the `HTTPRoute` that references the filter.

#### Values

- Default: `default`
- Data type: String

### `spec`

Map that contains the filter configuration. The `apiVersion`, `kind`, and `metadata` fields are siblings of the `spec` field. All other configurations are children.

### `spec.headerNames`

Specifies the names of the headers whose match conditions to negate in the rule that references the filter. Header names are not case sensitive.

#### Values

- Default: None
- This field is required.
- Data type: List of strings that contains at least one header name

## Example

In the following example, requests that include the `x-version` header with a value other than `v1` route to the `service-v2` service:

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1alpha1
kind: RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter
metadata:
  name: invert-version
  namespace: default
spec:
  headerNames:
    - x-version
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: version-route
  namespace: default
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: my-gateway
  rules:
  - matches:
    - headers:
      - type: Exact
        name: x-version
        value: v1
    filters:
    - type: ExtensionRef
      extensionRef:
        group: consul.hashicorp.com
        kind: RouteHeaderMatchInvertFilter
        name: invert-version
    backendRefs:
    - name: service-v2
      port: 80
```
